instagram.title: He Was Told He Would Serve. He Never Did.
instagram.description:
He was told he would serve. He never did.

"By your sword you shall live, And you shall serve your brother; And it shall come to pass, when you become restless, That you shall break his yoke from your neck." — Genesis 27:40

Isaac told Esau that he shall "serve" his brother.

Guess what? Esau never served Jacob in his lifetime.

What does that tell you? Esau refused to play to that decree. He chose his reality.

At that moment, he knew he had an option to serve or not to serve. He took responsibility for his own life.

The power may not necessarily be in what was said to you, but in how you have treated what was said to you.

If you allow the wrong mindset, you'll begin to live a life of defeat.

But you can choose to live against the narrative and walk in victory.

— Pst Emmanuel Omini

Swipe through 👉 then tell us in the comments: what word are you refusing to bow to this season?

facebook.title: Esau Was Told He Would Serve His Brother. He Never Did.
facebook.description:
Esau was told he would serve his brother. He never did — not once in his lifetime.

Read it for yourself:

"By your sword you shall live, And you shall serve your brother; And it shall come to pass, when you become restless, That you shall break his yoke from your neck." — Genesis 27:40

That was Isaac's word over Esau. And yet the record of Scripture is that Esau never served Jacob a single day of his life.

So what happened? Esau refused to play to that decree. In the moment he heard it, he understood something many believers never come to: he had an option. To serve, or not to serve. And he took responsibility for his own life.

Here is the lesson: the power may not necessarily be in what was said to you, but in how you have treated what was said to you.

If you allow the wrong mindset, you will begin to live a life of defeat. But you can choose to live against the narrative — and walk in victory.

— Pst Emmanuel Omini, The NewWine Place

Who needs to read this today? Share it with them, and tell us in the comments what word you are refusing to bow to this season.
